title: Texas's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Texas's 3rd Congressional District covers much of Collin County — including McKinney, Allen, and parts of Plano and Frisco — as well as most of Hunt County in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. The district has a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+10 and has been held by Republicans since 1968. Incumbent Republican Keith Self, a retired Army lieutenant colonel and former Collin County judge, is seeking a third term. He is being challenged by Democrat Evan Hunt, a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and defense executive who emphasizes his military service and positions on constitutional integrity, healthcare reform, and public education. The race takes place amid mid-decade redistricting litigation, though the Supreme Court has allowed Texas to use its new Republican-friendly congressional map for the 2026 elections.
polling_note: No district-specific opinion polls were found for Texas's 3rd Congressional District. Statewide generic ballot polls from the 2026 cycle show a competitive environment, but no TX-03 head-to-head polling is available.

candidates.name: Keith Self
candidates.summary: Keith Self is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and former Collin County judge, he serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee. Self is a conservative Republican who emphasizes border security, fiscal responsibility, and Second Amendment rights.

candidates.name: Evan Hunt
candidates.summary: Evan Hunt is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 3rd Congressional District, having advanced from the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary. A retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and combat aviator with 20 years of service, he later worked as a defense and aerospace executive at companies including Raytheon. Hunt's campaign focuses on defending the Constitution, protecting Social Security and Medicare, reforming healthcare, and strengthening public education.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific polling is available, so confidence is limited and the forecast relies on district fundamentals rather than head-to-head data. Those fundamentals strongly favor Republicans: TX-03 has a Cook PVI of R+10, has been held by Republicans since 1968, and incumbent Keith Self is seeking a third term in a Republican-friendly map that the Supreme Court allowed Texas to use for 2026. Democrat Evan Hunt is a credible challenger with military and executive credentials, but in an R+10 district without any polling showing a shift, Republicans retain a clear and substantial advantage — though not an overwhelming one, as a strong Democratic wave could theoretically narrow the margin.
